scope.description: Check the local predecessor-integrity relation across two actual handler invocations on the same receiver. Establish initially consistent stored history and metadata; the first invocation deletes an uncommitted conflicting suffix successfully and encounters a replacement-write error. Before any repair, deliver a subsequent otherwise admissible request naming the deleted cached endpoint. Compare its response with independently observed retained storage and snapshot metadata. This is a conditional interface-boundary check; legal sender-history reachability remains unresolved.
assumptions: Successful DeleteRange removes the inclusive requested suffix.
The selected fault case makes StoreLogs return an error without restoring the deleted predecessor; this is an explicit experiment condition, not an observed production-adapter behavior.
The deleted suffix is uncommitted, and the snapshot boundary lies strictly below the named deleted predecessor.
No intervening append, snapshot installation, restart, or metadata repair occurs between the two invocations.

The later request has an acceptable term and correctly formed fields. An empty Entries list and LeaderCommitIndex=0 isolate predecessor validation without claiming this sequence is generated by an ordinary leader.
excluded: Proof that a concrete production adapter realizes the injected failure
Proof of a legal distributed history generating both requests
Quorum support, commitment, application, client-visible loss, and overall consensus correctness
The separate post-storage configuration-processing failure branch
Crash durability of the test adapter

properties.reason: Actual result fields are compared after independent prerequisite association

adaptations: Construct an isolated receiver with consistent initial storage and metadata instead of starting a full node; no background processing runs.
Use a transport substitute solely for peer address encoding and decoding. Actual RPC.Respond delivers each response through a dedicated channel; network dispatch is excluded.
Inject the accepted conditional StoreLogs failure through a LogStore adapter after actual successful deletion. This does not characterize a production adapter.
Initialize configuration using the Config value representation demonstrated by NewRaft's conf.Store(*conf). Only configuration fields used by the exercised handler path are supplied.
Emit observations around actual target calls without modifying handler logic. The generated Go test leaves the forbidden-path comparison to the declared event property.
boundaries: Proof that a concrete production adapter realizes the injected failure
Proof of a legal distributed history generating both requests
Quorum support, commitment, application, client-visible loss, and overall consensus correctness
The separate post-storage configuration-processing failure branch
Crash durability of the test adapter
The injected adapter fault is conditional evidence, not an observation of production storage behavior.
The second request is tested at the receiving interface; its generation in a legal distributed sender history remains unresolved.
Direct invocation excludes concurrent node activity, transport dispatch, restart, snapshot installation, and intervening repair.
An empty-request response does not establish advancement of commitment.match, application, client-visible loss, or overall consensus failure.
The control's Go assertion is a test expectation for a retained matching predecessor; it is separate from the selected obligation comparison.

The error-producing store is an explicit fault adapter. InmemStore.StoreLogs itself always succeeds, and the supplied interface does not establish which production adapters exhibit the selected no-rollback failure semantics.

The harness bypasses NewRaft validation and startup, initializes only path-relevant receiver state, and supplies no functioning network transport, FSM or snapshot store. The review accepts this only for the declared isolated handler boundary, not as a constructor-valid deployment or an equivalent full-node execution.

The two requests are not evidence of a legal sender history. In particular, the same named term-2 sender first supplies term-2 replacements at indexes 2 and 3 and later names index 3 at term 1. The check does not explain how an ordinary leader generates that sequence. The supplied replication code derives predecessor terms from sender history and backs nextIndex down after rejection; header acceptance does not establish protocol-history legality.

The observed execution excludes intervening repair, restart, snapshot installation and concurrent node activity by construction. It does not establish whether full-node dispatch permits this sequence before repair.

An empty successful request does not advance nextIndex or commitment.match in the supplied updateLastAppended implementation. No quorum, commitment, application, client-visible loss or broader consensus consequence was observed.

This review covers the supplied check, harness and correlated execution only. The fixed scenario labels and prerequisite values are not a general-purpose monitor for arbitrary AppendEntries histories. The configuration-processing failure branch, snapshot-supported predecessors and other fault outcomes remain untested.

No formal model or calibration is required for this direct check, and none is inferred. The no-issue judgment concerns scoped semantic correspondence, not implementation correctness, independent replication of the experiment or resolution of unrelated semantic issues.
